text: Which type of genomic variant is defined as a single base-pair change and is the most common form of genetic variation?
explanation: A SNP is a single base change and is by far the most common type of genomic variation. Structural variants are rearrangements larger than 50 bp, CNVs are large duplications or deletions often exceeding 1 kb, and STR expansions involve changes in the number of repeat units — all are far less frequent than single-base substitutions.
